title: Sixth Word The Two Mens Responses And Outcomes

questions.question: In the story, what did the king give to each of the two men?
questions.answer: He gave each one an estate with the things needed to run it, like equipment, animals, and weapons.

questions.question: What was the condition of the time they were living in?
questions.answer: It was a dangerous time with war and trouble, so things did not stay safe or the same.

questions.question: Why did the king ask the two men to hand over what they were holding?
questions.answer: He wanted to protect it from being wasted or ruined.

questions.question: What did the king promise to do after the time of war ended?
questions.answer: He promised to give it back in a better condition than before.

questions.question: How did the king say he would treat the trust they handed over?
questions.answer: He said he would count it as their property and pay them well for it.

questions.question: What would happen to the tools and machines if the men accepted the king’s offer?
questions.answer: They would be used for the king’s work, and the return for using them would become much greater.

questions.question: Why did the king say the men should let him cover the costs?
questions.answer: Because they were poor and unable to handle such big expenses by themselves.

questions.question: What extra benefit did the king promise besides covering expenses?
questions.answer: He said he would also give them the income and profit.

questions.question: Until when would the men keep the property under this arrangement?
questions.answer: They would keep it until demobilization.

questions.question: What warning did the king give if they refused to sell?
questions.answer: They would not be able to protect what they had, and they would lose it.

questions.question: What would happen to the valuable tools and materials if they did not sell?
questions.answer: They would lose their worth.

questions.question: Besides losing their property, what other problem would they face if they refused?
questions.answer: They would carry the stress of taking care of it and also be punished for breaking trust.

questions.question: What new position would a man receive if he sold the property to the king?
questions.answer: He would become the king’s soldier and serve in the king’s name.

questions.question: How would that new position be better than being an ordinary captive or irregular fighter?
questions.answer: He would have an honored and freer rank under a great ruler.

questions.question: How did the wiser man respond to the message?
questions.answer: He gladly accepted it and was thankful.

questions.question: What kind of person was the second man shown to be?
questions.answer: He was proud, selfish, and careless.

questions.question: What false idea led the second man to reject the offer?
questions.answer: He acted as if he would remain on the estate forever.

questions.question: What happened to the first man in the end?
questions.answer: He rose to a high rank, gained the king’s favor, and lived happily.

questions.question: What happened to the second man in the end?
questions.answer: He lost his happiness and property and suffered punishment.

questions.question: Who brought the king’s message to the two men?
questions.answer: A noble lieutenant brought it.

questions.question: What does it mean that the property was “held in trust”?
questions.answer: It means the men were using it for a time, but it truly belonged to the king.

questions.question: Why was it not smart to cling tightly to the estate in that setting?
questions.answer: Because the time was unstable, and the estate could easily be destroyed or changed.

questions.question: What was one reason the king’s offer was merciful?
questions.answer: He offered to protect their property instead of letting it be lost.

questions.question: What did the king promise about the payment for the property?
questions.answer: He promised a high payment for it.

questions.question: How would the men benefit from letting their equipment be used for the king’s work?
questions.answer: They would receive much greater payment and benefit from it.

questions.question: What does the king’s offer show about his care for the two men?
questions.answer: It shows he cared for their needs and wanted good for them.

questions.question: Why could the men not properly manage the large expenses on their own?
questions.answer: Because they were needy and lacked resources.

questions.question: What would happen to the property if they tried to keep it by themselves?
questions.answer: They would still lose it because they could not preserve it.

questions.question: Why would refusing the offer be both foolish and harmful?
questions.answer: Because they would lose the property, miss the reward, and face punishment too.

questions.question: Which man showed wisdom through his response?
questions.answer: The first man did.

questions.question: What in his words shows that the first man accepted the offer with a good heart?
questions.answer: He said he was glad and grateful to accept it.

questions.question: What character flaw is strongest in the second man’s answer?
questions.answer: Pride is the strongest flaw in his answer.

questions.question: How did the second man’s attitude affect his judgment?
questions.answer: It made him ignore the dangers around him and refuse a better choice.

questions.question: What was the final result of the first man’s humble choice?
questions.answer: He gained honor, favor, and a happy life.

questions.question: What was the final result of the second man’s proud choice?
questions.answer: He ended up miserable, punished, and stripped of what he had.

questions.question: Why did people pity the second man but also say he deserved his state?
questions.answer: Because his suffering came from his own bad choice.

questions.question: What problem in the world made the king’s message urgent?
questions.answer: The world around them was full of war and instability.

questions.question: What was the king trying to stop from happening to the estate?
questions.answer: He was trying to stop it from being ruined or lost for no good reason.

questions.question: What does the king’s promise to return the estate in better shape show?
questions.answer: It shows generosity and care beyond simply taking it back.

questions.question: How would the men gain from the use of their workshop tools?
questions.answer: Their tools would be used in valuable work, and they would receive greatly increased return.

questions.question: Why is the king’s offer practical as well as generous?
questions.answer: It helps with both protection and all the costs of managing the estate.

questions.question: What burden would be lifted from the men if they accepted the offer?
questions.answer: They would no longer need to worry about paying the heavy expenses themselves.

questions.question: What kind of mistake would it be to trust their own power to save the property?
questions.answer: It would be a foolish mistake, because they were unable to keep it safe.

questions.question: How would selling the property change a man’s identity?
questions.answer: He would no longer be lowly and ordinary, but honored in the king’s service.

questions.question: Why is becoming the king’s soldier presented as an honor?
questions.answer: Because serving a great ruler in his name gives dignity and rank.

questions.question: What does the first man understand that the second man does not?
questions.answer: He understands that accepting the king’s offer leads to safety and reward.

questions.question: What wrong assumption did the second man make about life on the estate?
questions.answer: He acted as though it would last forever.

questions.question: How did love of enjoyment hurt the second man?
questions.answer: It made him reject what was truly better for him.

questions.question: What happened to the first man after some time passed?
questions.answer: He reached an honored position that others admired.

questions.question: Where did the first man end up living?
questions.answer: He lived happily in the king’s palace.

questions.question: What happened to the second man’s wealth and happiness?
questions.answer: Both were taken away from him.

questions.question: What feeling did people have when they looked at the second man?
questions.answer: They felt sorry for him, though they also knew his downfall came from his own mistake.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, what had the king placed under the care of the two men?
questions.answer: He had placed estates and their supplies under their care.

questions.question: Why were those possessions not secure?
questions.answer: Because the age was full of conflict and change.

questions.question: How did the king deliver his offer to the two men?
questions.answer: He sent a respected messenger with a kind decree.

questions.question: What was the king asking the men to do with what they were caring for?
questions.answer: He was asking them to hand it over to him willingly.

questions.question: What reason did the king give for making this request?
questions.answer: He wanted to keep it safe for them instead of letting it be wasted.

questions.question: What future promise made the offer especially hopeful?
questions.answer: The king promised to return it later in a better form.

questions.question: In what two ways did the king say they would be paid?
questions.answer: They would get a high payment and also profit from the use of their equipment.

questions.question: What does the king’s promise to handle expenses show about the men’s situation?
questions.answer: It shows they were not strong enough or rich enough to manage it alone.

questions.question: If the men refused, what would happen first to their possessions?
questions.answer: Their possessions would slip away and be lost.

questions.question: What would happen to the special tools and valuable materials if left as they were?
questions.answer: They would become useless and lose their worth.

questions.question: What two troubles would the men face if they did not accept the offer?
questions.answer: They would have the burden of guarding the trust and also face punishment.

questions.question: What better role was offered if a man agreed to the king’s terms?
questions.answer: He would become an honored soldier of the king.

questions.question: How did the first man react emotionally to the decree?
questions.answer: He felt happy, honored, and thankful.

questions.question: Which qualities caused the second man to refuse?
questions.answer: His pride, selfishness, and wasteful way of living caused him to refuse.

questions.question: How did the second man ignore the signs around him?
questions.answer: He paid no attention to the upheavals and acted as if nothing would end.

questions.question: What happened to the first man because of his choice?
questions.answer: He gained a high place and lived in comfort with the king’s favor.

questions.question: What happened to the second man because of his choice?
questions.answer: He fell into misery and punishment.

questions.question: Why is the ending of the story a strong contrast?
questions.answer: Because one man’s acceptance led to honor, while the other man’s refusal led to loss and suffering.

questions.question: What kind of ruler is shown in this parable?
questions.answer: He is shown as powerful, generous, and merciful.

questions.question: What kinds of things came with each estate?
questions.answer: Each estate came with working supplies and means for defense and use.

questions.question: Why was it unsafe to think those things would remain forever?
questions.answer: Because the world they lived in was unstable and full of destruction and change.

questions.question: What does the king’s request tell us about ownership?
questions.answer: It shows the men were caretakers, not the true owners.

questions.question: What was the king trying to save the men from?
questions.answer: He was trying to save them from pointless loss.

questions.question: What improvement did the king promise after the hard times ended?
questions.answer: He promised the property would be returned in better condition.

questions.question: What happened to the fee for using the tools if they accepted?
questions.answer: It would become far greater than before.

questions.question: Why was the king’s offer suited to the men’s weakness?
questions.answer: Because he took responsibility for the costs and equipment they could not handle.

questions.question: What shows that the offer was not only safe but also rewarding?
questions.answer: The king promised both protection and profit.

questions.question: If they refused, what would happen to the king’s high offer?
questions.answer: They would miss out on it completely.

questions.question: Why would their care for the estate become only trouble if they refused?
questions.answer: Because all their effort would still end in loss and punishment.

questions.question: How would accepting the offer raise their standing?
questions.answer: It would place them in honorable service under the king.

questions.question: Which man used better judgment right away?
questions.answer: The intelligent man did.

questions.question: How can we tell the first man did not feel forced?
questions.answer: He accepted gladly and with gratitude.

questions.question: What attitude made the second man speak as if the estate were truly his?
questions.answer: His arrogance made him speak that way.

questions.question: What desire did the second man not want to give up?
questions.answer: He did not want to give up his personal enjoyment.

questions.question: How is the first man’s ending described by others?
questions.answer: People envied his excellent condition.

questions.question: How is the second man’s ending described by others?
questions.answer: People pitied him and believed he had brought it on himself.

questions.question: What is one clear cause-and-effect lesson from the story?
questions.answer: Wise acceptance brings honor and happiness, while proud refusal brings loss and punishment.

questions.question: How many men are at the center of this parable, and what did they both receive?
questions.answer: There are two men, and both received an estate with many useful supplies.

questions.question: What made the estates hard to keep safe?
questions.answer: The time was full of turmoil, so nothing stayed secure.

questions.question: Who came from the king to explain what should be done?
questions.answer: A noble lieutenant came from the king.

questions.question: What was the main action the king asked the men to take?
questions.answer: He asked them to transfer the trust back to him.

questions.question: Why did the king say this was better than keeping it themselves?
questions.answer: Because he could preserve it for them, while they could not.

questions.question: What did the king say he would do with the property after the war?
questions.answer: He would return it in a better state.

questions.question: How did the king encourage them regarding the value of the trust?
questions.answer: He said he would count it as theirs and give a high return for it.

questions.question: What did the king promise concerning the workshop items?
questions.answer: He promised they would be used in his service and bring much greater benefit.

questions.question: Why would the king take over the costs and supplies?
questions.answer: Because the men were needy and not able to carry those burdens.

questions.question: What were the men still allowed to do with the property for a time?
questions.answer: They were allowed to keep it until the time of release from service.

questions.question: What would happen if they chose not to accept the king’s plan?
questions.answer: They would lose what they had and gain nothing from it.

questions.question: What does the passage say would happen to the fine tools and precious materials then?
questions.answer: They would become worthless.

questions.question: What two bad results came with trying to hold the trust wrongly?
questions.answer: There would be worry from managing it and punishment for unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What higher station came with agreeing to the king’s offer?
questions.answer: A man would serve as the king’s soldier in an honored way.

questions.question: What was the wise man’s answer to the decree?
questions.answer: He accepted it completely and with thanks.

questions.question: What inner problem ruled the second man?
questions.answer: His proud and selfish lower self ruled him.

questions.question: How did the second man misunderstand his situation?
questions.answer: He acted as if his stay in the estate would never end.

questions.question: What did the first man gain in the end besides material good?
questions.answer: He gained honor and the king’s favor.

questions.question: What did the second man lose in the end besides property?
questions.answer: He lost happiness and suffered torment.
